title: Universal self-similar evolution of two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates in the acoustic regime
authors: Guillaume Costa, Sergey Nazarenko, Giorgio Krstulovic
abstract: When driven out of equilibrium, a Bose-Einstein condensate develops nonlinearly interacting density waves that trigger a turbulent cascade, transferring energy toward small scales. In this article, we investigate the nonstationary evolution of solutions to the two-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Through numerical simulations of both the GPE and the corresponding Wave Kinetic Equation, we identify self-similar solutions relevant to atomic and polariton Bose-Einstein Condensates. These solutions exhibit characteristics of both first and second kind self-similarity. In particular, we show that the dynamics of the propagating front is universal, governed by a dimensionless universal constant $β$, which we determine numerically.
summary: This paper analyzes the turbulent decay of two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates by studying their energy spectrum evolution. Using both GPE simulations and the derived Wave Kinetic Equation, the authors prove that the system reaches a universal self-similar state. This finding quantifies how nonlinear wave interactions efficiently transfer energy to smaller length scales in these quantum gases.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonstationary, turbulent evolution of density waves in two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) when driven out of equilibrium.
main_result: The dynamics exhibit universal self-similar behavior characterized by a single constant $\beta$, suggesting that energy transfer towards small scales follows predictable scaling laws regardless of minor details.
method: The authors employ numerical simulations on the Gross-Pitaevskii Equation (GPE) and derive/solve the corresponding Wave Kinetic Equation (WKE) using self-similar ansatz solutions.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D BEC, modeled by the GPE. The analysis focuses on wave turbulence dynamics in the acoustic regime, where energy cascades from large to small scales.
key_observables: Energy spectrum $e_k$, the characteristic wavevector scale $k^*(t)$, and the universal constant $\beta$.
important_parameters: The system operates in the acoustic regime ($\xi \ll 1$), and the dynamics are characterized by initial energy $E_0$ and damping rates $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the validity of Weak Wave Turbulence Theory (WWTT) for this geometry, and approximations made when simplifying the collision integral in the WKE.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate snapshots showing structure formation, time evolution of $k^*$, and confirmation of self-similar dynamics by collapsing spectra onto master curves.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing GPE simulations to deriving the WKE, then solving for a self-similar ansatz solution $\Phi(\eta)$, leading to simplified differential equations whose asymptotic solutions yield the universal constant $\beta$.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, specifically characterizing how energy cascades in BECs through turbulence, which is crucial for understanding nonlinear wave physics in cold atom experiments.
